I was wondering why plastic wasn't already used for bullet casings like it is used for shotgun shells.

1) 12 gauge is around 12,000 psi max. 308 is around 62,000 psi.

2) 12 gauge uses ~16 grains of fast burning powder while .308 uses ~45 grains.

3) Shotshells fit loosely in the chamber which allows a bit of an air gap. Rifle and pistol ammo is fairly snug.

4) Plastic doesn't hold its shape very well compared to metal. This isn't a problem for shotguns which have such loose tolerances that they'll fire pretty much anything.

In the world of reloading, rifle and pistol reloading process is nearly identical. Meanwhile shotshells are entirely different. You don't have to clean or prep shotshells like you do brass.

On shotshells, if the metal base isn't damaged, and the plastic isn't split, you're good to go. No need to wipe the dirt off or lubricate the brass. Just replace the internals and crimp it shut. This is due to the loose and forgiving nature of shotguns, something rifles and pistols can't have if you want any kind of accuracy or precision.
